Decision-Process Opacity

The counterparty you can see fronts a coalition you cannot.

What it looks like Illustrative scenario

The plant manager said yes in the meeting and meant it. The deal then died in a room the platform never saw: a controller with a question nobody answered, a quality lead who heard about it third-hand. Nobody argued against it. Someone simply did not sign.

Scenario: The Match Argument

How an AI intervention works AI Trusted Intermediary · Content Match Story

Veto is cheaper than advocacy: a sceptic stalls by withholding assent, while a champion spends credibility to advance, and hidden influencers judge on second-hand, distorted information. The remedy is not to map the coalition. It is to route disclosure through a trusted intermediary both organizations accept, and to arm the champion with a Content Match Story: an evidence-weighted, sceptic-addressed document built to be forwarded, so the controller and every potential veto-holder read the case first-hand. The more portable it is, the less the deal is left to chance.

How traditional markets cope

  • The salesperson's relationship mapuntil the org chart changes
  • An executive sponsoruntil the sponsor moves on
  • Site visits and referencesuntil the person who matters never attends

What's new here

Quote tools and search engines serve one side. A narrative written for both parties at once, released only on mutual consent, has no documented equivalent.
